title: The bowline
summary: A fixed loop that doesn't slip and is easy to untie, even after loading.
steps: Make a small loop in the standing part, working end on top (“the rabbit hole”).
Pass the end of the rope up through this loop from underneath (“the rabbit comes out of the hole”).
Take the end around behind the standing part (“round the tree”).
Pass it back down into the small loop (“back down the hole”).
Tighten by pulling on the standing part while holding the big loop.
tips: Leave a free end of at least 10 times the rope's diameter.
Used to hoist a person or make a loop around the waist.

title: The clove hitch
summary: Quickly tie a rope to a post or branch.
steps: Wrap the rope once around the post.
Cross over the first turn and make a second turn.
Tuck the end under this second turn, between the rope and the post.
Tighten by pulling on both ends.
warnings: It can slip if the load changes: back it up with two half hitches for a heavy load.

title: The taut-line hitch (adjustable tension)
summary: To tension a tarp or tent guy line and adjust it.
steps: Pass the rope around the stake or tree.
With the end, make two turns around the standing part, towards the stake (inside the loop).
Make a third turn outside those two, on the opposite side.
Tighten: the knot slides when pushed, and locks under tension.

title: The reef knot (square knot)
summary: Join two ropes of the same diameter or close a bandage.
steps: Cross the right end over the left and tie a first overhand knot.
Cross the left end over the right and tie a second overhand knot.
Check: both ends come out on the same side, the knot is symmetrical.
warnings: Never use it to support a person or a heavy load: it can come undone.
